questions.question: What were the coins minted in Delhi during the reign of Tomar and Chauhan called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dehliwal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The coins minted in Delhi during the reign of the **Tomar** and **Chauhan dynasties** were called **Dehliwal**.
 
• The term "Dehliwal" specifically refers to the local coins produced in the Delhi region during the medieval period under the rule of these dynasties.
 
• These coins were primarily made of **silver** and were used as a medium of exchange in commerce and trade during that era.
 
• The Dehliwal coins played a significant role in the economic activities of northern India during the reign of the Tomars and Chauhans, symbolizing their administrative and monetary systems.
 
• The coins reflected **regional identity and sovereignty**, and their minting was a mark of local governance and control over trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tomar Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Tomar dynasty ruled Delhi before the Chauhan dynasty and was instrumental in establishing Delhi as a center of political and economic activity.
 
• They are credited with founding the city of **Delhi**, and their rule lasted until the Chauhans took over the region in the late 12th century.
 
• The reign of the Tomars witnessed significant developments in trade, and their coins like Dehliwal were widely used.
 
• The Tomar kings were known for their administrative capabilities and contributions to local governance.
 
 
 
• **Chauhan Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chauhans succeeded the Tomars in Delhi, with **Prithviraj Chauhan** being one of the most prominent rulers of the dynasty.
 
• The Chauhan dynasty played a crucial role in resisting invasions, especially from the **Ghurid Empire**.
 
• Dehliwal coins continued to be minted during their reign, reflecting the continuity of the monetary system established by the Tomars.
 
• Prithviraj Chauhan’s reign marked the last phase of the Chauhan dynasty before Delhi fell to Muslim rulers.
 
 
 
• **Other Coin Types:**
 
 
• **Rupees:** The term "Rupee" became prominent much later, especially during the Mughal and British periods, and does not pertain to the Tomar or Chauhan era.
 
• **Dinar:** Dinar was a gold coin used in the Middle East and parts of India, but it was not associated with the Tomars or Chauhans.
 
• **Tanka:** The Tanka was introduced by Muslim rulers after the Chauhan dynasty, particularly by the Delhi Sultanate, and was not relevant to the question.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Dehliwal Coins:**
 
 
• These coins were symbols of **regional autonomy** and governance under the Tomar and Chauhan rulers.
 
• The use of Dehliwal coins highlights the **economic and cultural significance** of Delhi during the medieval period.
 
• They represent the early monetary systems in India before the advent of centralized coinage by later dynasties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Tomar and Chauhan dynasties laid the foundation for Delhi’s prominence as a political and trade hub in northern India.
 
• The transition from Tomar to Chauhan rule marked a continuation of local governance systems, including coin minting practices.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The Dehliwal coins are an important artifact of early Indian history, providing insights into the economic systems of medieval India.
 
• They reflect the **cultural and political autonomy** of Delhi before the establishment of Muslim rule in the region.

questions.question: What was the 'zat' in the Mughal mansabdari system?

options.text: It determined the land a mansabdar was given.
It was the numerical value determining a noble's rank and salary.
It referred to the military responsibilities assigned to a noble.
It was a tax imposed on the mansabdars.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It was the numerical value determining a noble's rank and salary.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Zat** in the **Mughal Mansabdari system** referred to the numerical value assigned to each **mansabdar**, which determined their **rank** and **salary**.
 
• The rank was primarily categorized by the **Zat** number, which indicated the status and hierarchy of the noble within the Mughal administration.
 
• The **Zat** value also determined the financial remuneration a mansabdar would receive, thereby signifying their social and economic standing in the empire.
 
• Higher **Zat** numbers were associated with greater privileges, larger salaries, and higher administrative responsibilities.
 
• This system was introduced by **Akbar** and was an integral part of the administrative structure of the **Mughal Empire**, aiding in efficient governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mughal Mansabdari System:**

 
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was a unique administrative framework introduced by **Akbar** to manage the empire’s civil and military responsibilities.
 
• Under this system, every officer or noble was assigned a rank called **Mansab**, which was divided into two components: **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• **Zat** was the personal rank of the mansabdar, while **Sawar** denoted the number of horsemen a mansabdar was required to maintain for military service.
 
• The system aimed to ensure efficient administration and prevent hereditary claims to high-ranking positions.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Zat:**
 
 
• **Zat** was a numerical indicator of the noble's personal rank and the salary they would draw.
 
• It played a key role in determining the status of a mansabdar within the Mughal administrative hierarchy.
 
• The higher the **Zat** rank, the larger the jagir (land revenue assignment) granted to the individual.
 
• It ensured that nobles were paid adequately and maintained loyalty to the emperor.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Sawar:**
 
 
• While **Zat** defined rank and salary, **Sawar** defined the military obligations of a mansabdar.
 
• **Sawar** denoted the number of cavalry personnel a noble was required to maintain, which varied according to their rank and responsibilities.
 
• Both components were interlinked but served different purposes in the administration.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The system was crucial during the reign of **Akbar**, **Jahangir**, and **Shah Jahan**, helping to create a centralized bureaucracy.
 
• It eliminated feudal tendencies and ensured that administrative positions were merit-based rather than hereditary.
 
• It also helped maintain a stable military force, ensuring the empire's territorial integrity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zat ranks:**

 
 
• The **Zat** ranks ranged from **10** to **5000**, with higher ranks indicating greater influence and responsibilities.
 
• Ranks above **5000** were reserved for the highest-ranking officials and royal family members.
 
 
 
• **Jagir Allocation:**
 
 
• Based on the **Zat**, mansabdars were assigned **jagirs**, which were revenue-yielding lands to sustain their salaries and military expenses.
 
• This system ensured equitable distribution of resources and prevented concentration of power in the hands of a few nobles.
 
 
 
• **Akbar’s Reforms:**
 
 
• **Akbar** institutionalized the Mansabdari system as part of his broader administrative reforms to strengthen the Mughal Empire.
 
• He ensured that ranks were periodically reviewed, promoting efficiency and accountability among nobles.

questions.question: The Indian Ocean Rim Association was established in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)** was established in **1997** to promote regional cooperation and sustainable development within the Indian Ocean region.
 
• IORA was initiated by **India and South Africa** to create a platform for economic, socio-cultural, and political collaboration among countries bordering the Indian Ocean.
 
• The association's founding meeting took place in **Port Louis, Mauritius**, where the **Charter of the Indian Ocean Rim Association** was adopted.
 
• IORA aims to enhance **maritime security, trade facilitation, disaster management, scientific research**, and capacity building among its member states.
 
• It includes **23 member countries** from the Indian Ocean region and **10 dialogue partners**, which contribute to its objectives by providing expertise and resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Member Countries:**

 
 
• The IORA comprises **23 member states**, including countries like **India, Australia, Indonesia, South Africa, Sri Lanka, and the UAE**, among others.
 
• The organization includes countries that share a coastline with the **Indian Ocean**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of IORA:**
 
 
• Promoting **economic cooperation** and sustainable growth within the Indian Ocean region.
 
• Enhancing **maritime safety and security** to ensure freedom of navigation and secure trade routes.
 
• Encouraging **scientific and technological collaboration** for the development of member states.
 
• Strengthening **disaster risk management** by sharing expertise and resources.
 
 
 
• **Key Initiatives:**
 
 
• IORA plays a significant role in addressing issues like **illegal fishing, piracy, and maritime pollution**.
 
• The organization has launched the **Blue Economy Initiative**, focusing on sustainable use of ocean resources for economic growth, improved livelihoods, and ocean ecosystem health.
 
• It also conducts the annual **Indian Ocean Dialogue** to discuss regional cooperation and security challenges.
 
 
 
• **Structure of IORA:**
 
 
• The apex body of IORA is the **Council of Ministers (COM)**, consisting of foreign ministers from member states.
 
• The **Committee of Senior Officials (CSO)** supports the COM and oversees the implementation of decisions.
 
• The organization has a **Secretariat** based in **Ebène, Mauritius**, which coordinates activities and communication among member states.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Indian Ocean region is of strategic importance as it hosts some of the **busiest shipping lanes**, connecting the Middle East, Africa, and Asia.
 
• IORA promotes the concept of the **Blue Economy**, which includes sectors like fisheries, renewable energy, maritime transport, and tourism.
 
• IORA’s **Dialogue Partners** include countries like the United States, China, Japan, and Germany, which provide technical and financial assistance.
 
• The association is instrumental in fostering a **rules-based maritime order** in the Indian Ocean, aligning with international laws like the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)**.

questions.question: Who was first woman Chief Minister of any state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sucheta Kripalani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sucheta Kripalani** was the first woman Chief Minister of any state in India. She served as the Chief Minister of **Uttar Pradesh** from **1963 to 1967**.
 
• She was a prominent figure in the **Indian freedom struggle** and worked closely with Mahatma Gandhi during the **Quit India Movement**.
 
• Sucheta Kripalani represented **Indian National Congress**, the political party that played a pivotal role in India's independence and early governance.
 
• Her tenure as Chief Minister was marked by her efforts to improve administrative efficiency and address social issues, including those related to **women’s welfare and education**.
 
• She was known for her **determination and leadership**, especially during the **state employees' strike** in Uttar Pradesh, where she successfully negotiated and resolved the issues.
 
• She remains a symbol of **women's empowerment** in Indian politics, paving the way for future generations of female leaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other prominent women in Indian history:**

 
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali:** Known as the "Grand Old Lady" of the Indian Independence Movement, she played a pivotal role in the **Quit India Movement** and was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in 1997.
 
• **Anna Chandy:** She was the first woman judge in India and also one of the first women judges globally. She was appointed to the Kerala High Court in 1959.
 
• **Kamala Nehru:** She was the wife of Jawaharlal Nehru and a prominent freedom fighter, contributing to the **civil disobedience movement** and working for women’s rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Historical significance of women leaders:**
 
 
• Women leaders like Sucheta Kripalani paved the way for greater representation of women in Indian politics.
 
• Their contributions during the freedom struggle highlight their role in shaping India’s socio-political landscape.
 
• They have inspired initiatives for gender equality and efforts to empower women in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Key facts about Uttar Pradesh:**
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is India's most populous state and plays a significant role in the country's politics.
 
• It was the first state in India to have a **woman Chief Minister**, marking a milestone in Indian governance.
 
• It is known for its rich cultural heritage, historical landmarks, and diverse population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sucheta Kripalani’s legacy:**

 
 
• She was one of the few women leaders in Indian politics during the 20th century, making her achievements even more remarkable.
 
• Her work as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh set a precedent for future women leaders in Indian states.
 
• Her participation in the **freedom struggle** and dedication to public service showcased her commitment to India’s development.
 
 
 
• **Representation of women in Indian politics:**
 
 
• Women’s participation in politics has steadily increased since independence, with leaders like **Indira Gandhi** and **Pratibha Patil** holding key positions such as Prime Minister and President, respectively.
 
• Various laws and initiatives have been implemented to promote gender equality and increase women’s representation in governance.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first female recipient of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asima Chatterjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asima Chatterjee** was the first female recipient of the prestigious **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize** for Science and Technology in **1961**, awarded for her contributions to the field of organic chemistry.
 
• She is renowned for her groundbreaking work in the fields of **medicinal chemistry**, especially for her research on **alkaloids** and the development of anti-malarial and anti-epileptic drugs.
 
• Her research primarily revolved around the **chemistry of natural products**, including plant-based substances, which have significant applications in medicine.
 
• Asima Chatterjee made significant contributions to **Indian science**, becoming a trailblazer for women scientists in the country.
 
• The **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize**, established in **1958**, is one of India’s highest science awards, given annually by the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)** for outstanding contributions to science and technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize:**

 
 
• Named after **Dr. Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar**, the founder Director of CSIR, the prize recognizes exceptional achievements in various fields of science like **Biological Sciences, Engineering, Mathematics, Medicine, Physical Sciences, and Chemical Sciences**.
 
• Each award includes a citation, a plaque, and a cash prize of **₹5 lakh**.
 
• The prize is awarded to scientists below the age of **45 years** for their contributions to Indian science.
 
 
 
• **Asima Chatterjee’s Legacy:**
 
 
• Born on **23 September 1917** in Kolkata, she became the **first woman to earn a Doctorate of Science** from an Indian university (University of Calcutta).
 
• She served as the **Chairperson of the Chemistry Department** at Lady Brabourne College, Kolkata.
 
• Her pioneering work on **natural products** chemistry contributed significantly to drug development, especially in the areas of **malaria, epilepsy, and cancer**.
 
• She was awarded the **Padma Bhushan** in **1975** for her contributions to science.
 
 
 
• **Other female recipients of the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize:**
 
 
• After Asima Chatterjee, other women scientists like **Sudipta Sengupta** (1983, Earth Sciences) and **Archana Bhattacharyya** (1998, Physical Sciences) have also received this prestigious award.
 
• This highlights the growing recognition of women in Indian science over the decades.
 
 
 
• **Important Contributions of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Debala Mitra:** An eminent Indian archaeologist who served as the Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI). Her work focuses on ancient Indian monuments but she did not receive the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize.
 
• **Sudipta Sengupta:** A distinguished geologist who received the prize in **1983** for her work in Earth Sciences. However, she was not the first female recipient.
 
• **Archana Bhattacharyya:** A physicist who received the prize in **1998** for her contributions to space physics but was not the first woman to receive it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gender Representation in Science:**

 
 
• Women’s contributions in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics) fields in India have historically been underrepresented.
 
• Awards like the **Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize** encourage greater participation and recognition of women in scientific research.
 
• Efforts by institutions like CSIR to promote diversity and inclusion in science are crucial for breaking gender barriers.
 
 
 
• **Encouragement for Research:**
 
 
• Such prestigious awards provide motivation for young scientists to pursue innovative research.
 
• They also highlight the importance of focusing on indigenous scientific advancements.

questions.question: In 2024, at the National Film Awards, the Best Music Direction (Songs) award was presented to ______ for his work on Brahmastra - Part 1: Shiva (Hindi).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pritam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pritam**, one of India’s leading music directors, won the **Best Music Direction (Songs)** award at the **National Film Awards 2024** for his remarkable work in the Hindi movie **Brahmastra - Part 1: Shiva**.
 
• Pritam is known for his versatile music composition and has been instrumental in delivering chart-topping songs in Bollywood. His work in Brahmastra was widely appreciated for blending modern and traditional musical elements seamlessly.
 
• The soundtrack of **Brahmastra - Part 1: Shiva** featured several hit songs such as *Kesariya*, *Deva Deva*, and *Rasiya*, which became instant favorites among audiences and critics alike.
 
• This award adds to Pritam’s illustrious career, which includes multiple awards like Filmfare Awards, IIFA Awards, and Zee Cine Awards for his exceptional contributions to Indian cinema.
 
• The National Film Awards, considered one of the most prestigious awards in Indian cinema, recognize excellence across various categories, including acting, direction, cinematography, and music composition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pritam Chakraborty:**

 
 
• Pritam was born on **14 June 1971** in **Kolkata, West Bengal**, India. He is a prominent Indian composer and playback singer.
 
• He is known for his ability to experiment with diverse genres, including pop, rock, classical, and traditional Indian music.
 
• Pritam has worked on numerous blockbuster movies such as **Barfi!**, **Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani**, **Dilwale**, and **Jab We Met**.
 
• He is often praised for his ability to connect with audiences across different age groups through his memorable and melodious compositions.
 
 
 
• **Brahmastra - Part 1: Shiva:**
 
 
• It is a Hindi-language fantasy adventure movie directed by **Ayan Mukerji** and produced by **Karan Johar** under the banner of Dharma Productions.
 
• Released in **2022**, the film stars **Ranbir Kapoor**, **Alia Bhatt**, **Amitabh Bachchan**, **Nagarjuna Akkineni**, and **Mouni Roy**.
 
• The movie revolves around the concept of astras (weapons of power) and combines elements of Indian mythology with modern-day storytelling.
 
• The music of the film played a pivotal role in enhancing its narrative and emotional appeal.
 
 
 
• **National Film Awards:**
 
 
• The **National Film Awards** are presented annually by the **Directorate of Film Festivals**, an organization under the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting**, Government of India.
 
• Established in **1954**, these awards aim to encourage and honor excellence in Indian cinema across various languages and categories.
 
• Winners are selected by a national jury consisting of eminent personalities from the Indian film industry.
 
• The awards include categories like Best Actor, Best Actress, Best Director, Best Feature Film, and Best Music Direction, among others.
 
 
 
• **Other Nominees for the Category:**
 
 
• While Pritam won the award, other notable music directors like **Mahesh Bhuvanend**, **Niki Joshi**, and **Ravi Varman** were also recognized for their contributions in different films.
 
• However, Pritam’s work stood out for its innovation, emotional depth, and widespread popularity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kesariya:**

 
 
• The song *Kesariya* from Brahmastra became a massive hit and garnered millions of views on YouTube within days of its release.
 
• Its soulful lyrics and melodious composition contributed significantly to the film’s popularity.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Music in Indian Cinema:**
 
 
• Music plays a crucial role in Indian films, often driving the narrative and connecting emotionally with audiences.
 
• The National Film Awards honor exceptional contributions in music direction, highlighting its importance in the cinematic experience.

questions.question: 50th Statehood Day of a state was celebrated in May 2025. Prem Singh Tamang (P.S. Golay) is Chief Minister of this state. Which state is being discussed here?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sikkim** celebrated its **50th Statehood Day** in May 2025, marking five decades since it officially became a part of India.
 
• Sikkim was granted **statehood on May 16, 1975**, through the **36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975**, making it the 22nd state of India.
 
• The current Chief Minister of Sikkim is **Prem Singh Tamang**, also known as **P.S. Golay**. He has been serving as the Chief Minister since **May 2019**.
 
• Prior to its statehood, Sikkim was a **protectorate of India** and governed as per the Indo-Sikkim Treaty of 1950.
 
• Sikkim is renowned for being India’s **smallest state by population** and for its unique geographical and cultural diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background of Sikkim:**

 
 
• Sikkim was ruled by the **Namgyal dynasty** before becoming a protectorate under India in 1950.
 
• The **Indo-Sikkim Treaty of 1950** ensured that India controlled its defense, communication, and external affairs.
 
• In **1975**, a referendum was held, and the majority of Sikkimese people voted to abolish the monarchy and merge with India.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance:**
 
 
• Sikkim is located in the northeastern part of India, bordered by **Nepal, Bhutan, China, and West Bengal**.
 
• It is home to **Kangchenjunga**, the third-highest mountain in the world and a sacred peak for the Sikkimese people.
 
• Despite being the **second smallest state** by area, Sikkim is known for its biodiversity, hosting a wide range of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Prem Singh Tamang (P.S. Golay):**
 
 
• Prem Singh Tamang is the leader of the **Sikkim Krantikari Morcha (SKM)** party.
 
• He took office as the Chief Minister of Sikkim on **May 27, 2019**, after his party won the state elections.
 
• Golay has been pivotal in implementing several developmental projects in Sikkim, focusing on tourism, education, and environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim’s Achievements:**
 
 
• Sikkim was declared **India’s first organic state** in 2016, promoting sustainable agricultural practices.
 
• The state is also recognized for its **high literacy rate** and efforts in preserving its **indigenous culture**.
 
• It is a popular tourist destination due to its **natural beauty**, monasteries, and adventure opportunities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **36th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1975:**

 
 
• This amendment officially **integrated Sikkim** into India as a full-fledged state.
 
• It added **Article 371F** to the Indian Constitution, providing special provisions to protect Sikkim’s cultural and social heritage.
 
 
 
• **Tourism in Sikkim:**
 
 
• Sikkim attracts tourists with destinations like **Tsomgo Lake, Nathula Pass, Rumtek Monastery, and Yumthang Valley**.
 
• The state actively promotes **eco-tourism** and sustainable travel practices.
 
 
 
• **Sikkim’s Role in India:**
 
 
• Sikkim serves as a strategic location due to its proximity to international borders, especially with China.
 
• The Indian Army maintains a significant presence in Sikkim to safeguard national security.

questions.question: In July 2024, which country recently conferred its highest civilian award "The Order of St. Andrew the Apostle" to Prime Minister Narendra Modi?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** was recently conferred with Russia's highest civilian honor, **"The Order of St. Andrew the Apostle,"** in recognition of his exceptional contributions towards strengthening bilateral relations between India and Russia.

questions.question: According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24, India's overall female labour force participation rate (FLFPR) has risen to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.417**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2023-24** is a comprehensive survey conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** of India under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). It monitors employment and labour force trends.
 
• According to the **PLFS 2023-24**, the **female labour force participation rate (FLFPR)** in India has increased to **41.7% (0.417)**. This marks a significant improvement in women's participation in the workforce.
 
• The **FLFPR** refers to the proportion of women aged 15 years and above who are either working (employed) or seeking work (unemployed) relative to the total female population in the same age group.
 
• This increase highlights the positive impact of government initiatives, skill development programs, and increased awareness of gender equality in workplaces.
 
• Despite this growth, India's FLFPR is still lower than the global average, indicating the need for further policy measures and reforms to enhance women's employment opportunities.

questions.question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, a revamped UDAN initiative will be launched to further enhance regional connectivity, adding ______ new destinations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**120**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **Union Budget 2025-26**, the government of India has announced a revamped version of the **UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) initiative**. The initiative is aimed at enhancing **regional air connectivity**.
 
• The revamped UDAN initiative will add **120 new destinations** to its network, further expanding the accessibility of air travel to remote and underserved areas of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UDAN Scheme Overview:**

 
 
• The **UDAN scheme** was launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in **2016** under the **Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS)**.
 
• It aims to **connect unserved and underserved airports** across India and make air travel affordable for the public.
 
• Under the scheme, financial incentives are provided to airlines in the form of **Viability Gap Funding (VGF)**, ensuring affordable ticket pricing.
 
 
 
• **Original Impact of the UDAN Scheme:**
 
 
• Since its inception, the UDAN scheme has connected over **70 airports**, with **1 crore passengers** benefitting from affordable flights.
 
• Key routes have been established connecting **Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities** to major metropolitan hubs.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Allocation for the Revamped Scheme:**
 
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** has allocated significant funding for the revamped UDAN initiative to ensure the expansion of **regional aviation infrastructure**.
 
• The government has promised to enhance **airport infrastructure** and operational capabilities in smaller cities.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Benefits:**

• Improved air connectivity will benefit industries such as **agriculture, trade, and logistics**, fostering growth in remote areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Viability Gap Funding (VGF):**

 
 
• VGF is a financial support mechanism provided by the government to compensate for the **shortfall in revenue** for airlines operating under the UDAN scheme.
 
• This ensures that ticket prices remain affordable for passengers while airlines remain financially viable.
 
 
 
• **Unserved and Underserved Airports:**
 
 
• Unserved airports are those with no scheduled commercial flights, while underserved airports have limited connectivity.
 
• The revamped UDAN scheme prioritizes the development and operationalization of these airports.
 
 
 
• **Focus on Sustainable Aviation:**

questions.question:
Narcotics are used as doping in sports. Which of the following is an example of narcotics?

I. Morphine 

II. Methadone
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narcotics** are substances that act on the central nervous system to relieve pain or induce sleep but have a high potential for abuse and addiction. Examples include Morphine and Methadone.
 
• **Morphine:** It is a potent opioid analgesic derived from the opium plant and is widely used for pain relief in medical settings. It also falls under the category of narcotics and is banned in sports as it enhances performance by masking pain. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• **Methadone:** Methadone is a synthetic opioid used to treat severe pain and as part of drug addiction detoxification. It is classified as a narcotic and is prohibited in sports due to its potential for abuse and performance-enhancing effects. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• Narcotics are listed as prohibited substances under the guidelines of the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA).**
 
• The use of narcotics in sports violates fair play principles and poses significant health risks to athletes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Morphine:**

 
 
• Morphine is derived from the resin of the opium poppy (*Papaver somniferum*).
 
• It is used for managing severe pain in conditions like post-surgery recovery or terminal illnesses such as cancer.
 
• Morphine binds to opioid receptors in the brain and spinal cord, altering the perception of pain.
 
• It can cause side effects such as sedation, respiratory depression, and addiction.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Methadone:**
 
 
• Methadone is a synthetic opioid developed in **Germany during World War II**.
 
• It is used for pain management and as a substitute for heroin in drug addiction treatment.
 
• Methadone works by blocking the euphoric effects of narcotics, thereby reducing cravings and withdrawal symptoms.
 
• It is administered under strict medical supervision due to its high addiction potential.
 
 
 
• **Regulations in Sports:**
 
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** maintains a list of prohibited substances, including narcotics, to ensure fair competition.
 
• Athletes found using banned substances face consequences such as disqualification, suspension, or fines.
 
• Doping tests are conducted during competitions and training to detect the use of narcotics.
 
 
 
• **Health Risks of Narcotics:**
 
 
• Narcotics can lead to addiction, tolerance, and dependence, making them hazardous for long-term use.
 
• Overdose can cause respiratory failure, coma, or even death.
 
• Prolonged use may result in psychological issues such as depression or anxiety.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA):**

 
 
• WADA was established in **1999** to combat doping in sports globally.
 
• It publishes the **Prohibited List** annually, which includes narcotics, stimulants, and other performance-enhancing substances.
 
• WADA promotes education and awareness to discourage athletes from engaging in doping.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Narcotics Prohibited in Sports:**
 
 
• Morphine
 
• Methadone
 
• Heroin
 
• Codeine (in certain concentrations)
 
 
 
• **Consequences of Doping:**
 
 
• Disqualification from competitions
 
• Damage to reputation
 
• Legal penalties in certain jurisdictions
 
• Long-term health complications

questions.question: A badminton match generally consists games of ______ points each.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21 points**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A badminton match generally consists of games played up to **21 points** under the **rally scoring system**.
 
• In the rally scoring system, a point is awarded for every rally, regardless of which player serves. 
 
• The player or team that first reaches **21 points** wins the game, provided they have a lead of at least **two points** over their opponent.
 
• If the score reaches **20-20**, the game continues until one player/team achieves a lead of **two points**, but the maximum score limit is **30 points**. This means the first player/team to reach **30 points** wins the game.
 
• A badminton match typically consists of **three games**, and the player or team that wins **two out of three games** is declared the winner. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scoring System:**

 
 
• The rally scoring system was introduced in **2006** by the **Badminton World Federation (BWF)** to make the game faster and more exciting.
 
• Under this system, players can score points regardless of who is serving.
 
• Each game is played to **21 points**, with the winner requiring at least a two-point lead unless the score reaches **30-29**.
 
 
 
• **Badminton Match Format:**
 
 
• A standard badminton match consists of **three games**, referred to as the **best of three**.
 
• The player or team that wins two games first is declared the match winner.
 
• The match can end in straight sets if one player/team wins the first two games.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Prior to 2006, the scoring system varied, with games played to **15 points** for men’s singles and doubles, and **11 points** for women’s singles.
 
• The transition to the rally scoring system was made to increase the pace of the game and improve its appeal for spectators and broadcasters.
 
 
 
• **Major Badminton Championships:**
 
 
• Badminton is governed internationally by the **Badminton World Federation (BWF)**.
 
• Prominent tournaments include the **All England Championships**, the **Olympic Games**, and the **BWF World Championships**.
 
• Badminton is immensely popular in countries such as **China**, **India**, **Indonesia**, and **Denmark**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Rules:**

 
 
• A player/team changes sides at the end of each game and during the third game when one side reaches **11 points**.
 
• The interval between games lasts **two minutes**, and players are allowed a **60-second break** when one side scores **11 points** in a game.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Insights:**
 
 
• Players often adjust their strategy based on the rally scoring system to maximize points during service and return.
 
• Game pace and endurance play a vital role, as matches can be physically demanding under the **21-point system**.
 
 
 
• **Sportsmanship:**
 
 
• Players are expected to adhere to fair play principles and respect the umpire’s decisions.
 
• Badminton emphasizes agility, precision, and tactical gameplay, making it a sport of both physical and mental skill.

questions.question: What is the name of Blue Origin's first orbital rocket launched in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Glenn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **New Glenn** is the first orbital-class rocket developed by Blue Origin, a private aerospace manufacturer and spaceflight services company founded by **Jeff Bezos** in the year **2000**.
 
• The rocket is named after **John Glenn**, the first American astronaut to orbit the Earth, signifying its mission to achieve orbital spaceflight capabilities.
 
• **Blue Origin** launched the **New Glenn** rocket in **January 2025**, marking a major milestone in its efforts to compete with other spaceflight companies like SpaceX.
 
• The rocket is a **two-stage launch vehicle** designed for a wide range of missions, including satellite deployment and interplanetary exploration.
 
• New Glenn features a reusable first stage that is capable of landing on a ship at sea, reducing costs and making spaceflight more sustainable.
 
• The rocket is powered by **BE-4 engines**, developed in-house by Blue Origin, and uses liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquid oxygen (LOX) as propellants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **New Shepard**:

 
 
• New Shepard is a suborbital rocket developed by Blue Origin for **space tourism** and scientific payloads.
 
• It is named after **Alan Shepard**, the first American astronaut to travel to space.
 
• The rocket is designed to carry passengers and experiments to the **Kármán line**, the boundary of space, and return safely to Earth.
 
• Unlike New Glenn, it is not intended for orbital missions but focuses on short-duration suborbital flights.
 
 
 
• **New Horizon**:
 
 
• New Horizon is not related to Blue Origin but is a **NASA spacecraft** launched in 2006.
 
• It was designed for the exploration of **Pluto** and the **Kuiper Belt**, making it one of NASA's most successful interplanetary missions.
 
• This option is unrelated to the orbital capabilities of Blue Origin rockets.
 
 
 
• **Blue Moon**:
 
 
• Blue Moon is a **lunar lander** developed by Blue Origin as part of its goal to support NASA's **Artemis program** for returning humans to the Moon.
 
• It is designed to deliver cargo and possibly crew to the lunar surface, focusing on lunar exploration and development.
 
• It is not an orbital rocket but a specialized lander for Moon missions.
 
 
 
• **Features and Capabilities of New Glenn:**
 
 
• The rocket has a massive payload capacity of up to **45 metric tons** to low Earth orbit (LEO), making it suitable for heavy payloads.
 
• Its reusable first stage can perform **up to 25 missions**, significantly reducing operational costs.
 
• The rocket's design includes a seven-meter fairing, providing ample space for satellites and other payloads.
 
• New Glenn's first stage recovery mechanism is similar to SpaceX's Falcon 9, enabling it to land on a floating platform at sea.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **BE-4 Engine:**

 
 
• The BE-4 engine is a state-of-the-art rocket engine developed by Blue Origin to power both New Glenn and United Launch Alliance's **Vulcan Centaur**.
 
• It uses **methane** as fuel, making it more efficient and environmentally friendly compared to traditional kerosene-based engines.
 
 
 
• **Competition:**
 
 
• New Glenn is positioned to compete with SpaceX's **Falcon Heavy** and **Starship**, as well as ULA's Vulcan Centaur, in the commercial spaceflight market.
 
• Its large payload capacity and reusability make it attractive for satellite deployment and interplanetary missions.
 
 
 
• **Blue Origin’s Vision:**
 
 
• Blue Origin aims to create a future where millions of people live and work in space, focusing on **reusability** and sustainability in space exploration.
 
• New Glenn is a stepping stone toward achieving this vision, aligning with the company's motto: "**Gradatim Ferociter**" (Step by Step, Ferociously).

questions.question: Why we are not crushed under the large atmospheric pressure?

options.text: Because atmospheric pressure is very low
Because the pressure inside our body balances the outside pressure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because the pressure inside our body balances the outside pressure.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atmospheric pressure** at sea level is approximately **101.3 kPa (kilopascals)** or **1 atmosphere (atm)**. This is a significant force, yet humans do not feel crushed under it because the pressure inside the body matches this external atmospheric pressure.
 
• The **human body** is equipped with **fluid-filled organs, tissues, and cells** that maintain an internal pressure equal to the external atmospheric pressure. This balance prevents any crushing effect.
 
• Our bodies are not rigid; they are **flexible and adaptive**. The fluids and gases inside our body, such as blood and air in the lungs, exert an outward pressure that **counterbalances the atmospheric pressure**.
 
• When there is a sudden change in atmospheric pressure, such as during high-altitude travel or deep-sea diving, the body may feel discomfort (e.g., ear popping), but it usually adjusts to the new pressure over time. This is due to mechanisms like the **Eustachian tube** in the ear.
 
• The concept of pressure balancing is a fundamental principle in physics and biology. Without this balance, humans would not be able to survive under such high atmospheric pressure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure:**

 
 
• It is the force exerted by the weight of the atmosphere on any surface.
 
• Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately **101,325 Pascals (Pa)** or 760 mmHg (millimeters of mercury).
 
• It decreases with increasing altitude and increases with depth in water or other fluids.
 
 
 
• **Internal Body Pressure:**
 
 
• The human body maintains an internal pressure that matches the external atmospheric pressure, preventing any imbalance.
 
• This equilibrium is maintained by the **circulatory system, respiratory system, and tissue fluids**.
 
 
 
• **Decompression and Pressure Variations:**
 
 
• Sudden changes in external pressure can lead to conditions like **barotrauma** or **decompression sickness**.
 
• For example, divers ascending too quickly may experience **"the bends"** due to nitrogen bubbles forming in their blood.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Pressure Balancing:**
 
 
• Pressure-suited environments, such as spacesuits or submarines, are designed to **mimic atmospheric conditions** to keep the human body safe.
 
• Medical devices like **hyperbaric oxygen chambers** utilize controlled pressure to treat certain conditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Because we are very strong" – This is incorrect because physical strength has no influence on resisting atmospheric pressure. The balance is due to internal and external pressure equilibrium.
 
• **Option 2:** "Because gravity pulls it away" – Incorrect as gravity plays a role in the existence of atmospheric pressure but does not pull it away to prevent crushing.
 
• **Option 3:** "Because atmospheric pressure is very low" – Incorrect because atmospheric pressure is not low; it is significant (101.3 kPa at sea level). The body’s internal pressure balances it out.
 
• **Option 4:** "Because the pressure inside our body balances the outside pressure" – Correct as the internal and external pressures are in equilibrium, preventing any crushing effect.

questions.question: The grammar composed by Panini consists of over ______ grammatical rules.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panini**, an ancient Indian scholar, composed one of the most comprehensive and scientific grammatical frameworks for the **Sanskrit language**.
 
• The grammar system developed by Panini is called **Ashtadhyayi**, which translates to "Eight Chapters."
 
• The **Ashtadhyayi** consists of approximately **4000 sutras (grammatical rules)** that systematically describe the structure, phonetics, and syntax of Sanskrit.
 
• Panini’s grammar is widely regarded as the **foundation of linguistic studies** and has influenced both ancient and modern language sciences.
 
• The rules are written in **concise aphoristic style**, making them compact yet highly detailed, suitable for oral transmission in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Panini's Life:**

 
 
• Panini is believed to have lived in **ancient India** around the 5th to 4th century BCE.
 
• He hailed from the region near present-day **Gandhara** (modern Pakistan and Afghanistan).
 
 
 
• **Ashtadhyayi's Structure:**
 
 
• The Ashtadhyayi is divided into **eight chapters**, each containing several sections.
 
• It covers **phonology**, **morphology**, and **syntax**, providing a complete linguistic framework.
 
• The sutras are organized to ensure minimal redundancy and maximum clarity.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Approach:**
 
 
• Panini's grammar employs a highly **formalized structure**, resembling modern computational linguistics.
 
• It uses **meta-rules and auxiliary markers** to simplify complex grammatical patterns.
 
 
 
• **Influence on Linguistics:**
 
 
• Panini’s work has had a profound impact on linguistic theories, including the development of **formal language theory**.
 
• His methodologies have inspired modern linguists like **Noam Chomsky**.
 
 
 
• **Application of Ashtadhyayi:**
 
 
• The grammar is still studied and used by **scholars of Sanskrit**, linguistics, and computational language modeling.
 
• It serves as a cornerstone for understanding classical texts and teaching Sanskrit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy:** Panini’s grammar remains one of the earliest and most sophisticated examples of linguistic analysis.
 
• **Historical Context:** The Ashtadhyayi was composed during a time when oral traditions dominated, emphasizing brevity and precision.
 
• **Global Recognition:** Panini is often referred to as the "father of linguistics" due to his pioneering work.
 
• **Modern Studies:** Scholars continue to explore Panini’s methods to enhance computational linguistics and artificial intelligence.
